subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit delegate-only/self-deny policy for requester agents, and what public config shape should own it?
rationale: Source proves the missing capability, but the fix changes public config and the security semantics of how tool deny/allow policy inherits across parent and child agents.

options.title: Add delegate-only config
options.body: Introduce an optional per-agent self-deny/delegate-only equivalent that hides tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins and controlled subagent inheritance.

options.title: Rely on per-spawn child policy
options.body: Treat #15032/#78441-style toolsAllow as the supported path for child narrowing and document that parent direct-use prevention remains outside scope.

options.title: Keep monotonic policy
options.body: Reject delegate-only inheritance for now and document separate-agent or operator-boundary workarounds as the supported security model.

recommendation.title: Add delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Introduce an optional per-agent self-deny/delegate-only equivalent that hides tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins and controlled subagent inheritance.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent/subagent policy and docs work makes this the best available owner for the product/security contract choice.
